llm_narrative: Across the 500 evaluation tasks the granite4.1_3b_output model achieved a mean claim‑coverage of only 0.0706 (≈7 % of expected facts) and a median of zero, with just 1.6 % of runs reaching the 75 % coverage threshold. Failure diagnostics were recorded for 496 instances (99.2 % of the sample), split between tool‑call problems (191 cases, 38.5 %) and purely cognitive errors (305 cases, 61.5 %). The three most common root causes were task misunderstanding (147 occurrences), failure to invoke any MCP tools (141 occurrences), and early termination after one or two calls (88 occurrences), together accounting for roughly 75 % of all failures. This pattern shows that the model frequently mis‑interprets multi‑step prompts, assumes it lacks access to required data, and then aborts before synthesising retrieved information, rather than struggling with tool syntax itself. A concrete remediation is to prepend a “tool‑use checklist” prompt that forces the model to (1) enumerate each required piece of evidence, (2) map each to a specific MCP tool, and (3) confirm completion before generating the final answer. Compared with other models, granite4.1_3b_output’s failure profile is distinguished by an unusually high proportion of cognitive breakdowns—especially task‑misunderstanding and premature exit—while its raw tool‑call success rate remains relatively respectable.
